description: Standardized evaluation dataset for MedPaperPulse-AI (MedLit Explorer). Contains 12 real PubMed abstracts and 4 synthetic edge-case abstracts.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine

passages.text: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes coronavirus disease 2019 (Covid-19).
In an ongoing multinomial trial, we randomly assigned persons 16 years of age or older in a 1:1 ratio to receive two doses of BNT162b2 (30 ug per dose) or placebo 21 days apart.
A total of 43,548 participants underwent randomization across international sites.
There were 8 cases of Covid-19 with onset at least 7 days after the second dose among participants assigned to BNT162b2 and 162 cases among those assigned to placebo.
BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing Covid-19 (95% credible interval, 90.3 to 97.6).
The safety profile was characterized by short-term, mild-to-moderate pain at the injection site, fatigue, and headache.
A two-dose regimen of BNT162b2 conferred 95% protection against Covid-19 in persons 16 years of age or older.

pico.population: Persons 16 years of age or older

records.title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity

passages.text: Obesity is a chronic disease requiring potent pharmacological therapies for sustained weight reduction.
In this phase 3 double-blind trial, 2539 adults with a BMI of 30 or higher were assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg) or placebo once weekly for 72 weeks.
The mean percentage change in weight at week 72 was -15.0% with 5-mg doses, -19.5% with 10-mg doses, -20.9% with 15-mg doses, and -3.1% with placebo (P<0.001 for all comparisons).
The most common adverse events with tirzepatide were gastrointestinal events, which were primarily mild to moderate in severity.
In this 72-week trial in participants with obesity, 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg of tirzepatide once weekly provided substantial and sustained reductions in body weight.

pico.population: 2539 adults with BMI of 30 or higher
pico.outcome: Mean percentage weight reduction at week 72

records.title: Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction

passages.text: In patients with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors reduce the risk of hospitalization for heart failure.
In this phase 3 trial, 4744 patients with NYHA class II to IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less were randomized to dapagliflozin 10 mg daily or placebo.
The primary outcome occurred in 386 of 2373 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 502 of 2371 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (HR 0.74; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001).
Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 9.6% in the dapagliflozin group and 11.5% in the placebo group (HR 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98).
Among patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction, dapagliflozin lowered the risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death.

pico.outcome: Worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death

records.title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

passages.text: First-line therapy for metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) lacking targetable mutations is chemotherapy.
In this double-blind trial, 616 patients with untreated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC were randomly assigned (2:1) to pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum or placebo plus chemotherapy.

At a median follow-up of 10.5 months, the estimated rate of overall survival at 12 months was 69.2% in the pembrolizumab combination group versus 49.4% in the placebo combination group (HR for death 0.49; 95% CI 0.38 to 0.64; P<0.001).
Median progression-free survival was 8.8 months in the pembrolizumab group compared to 4.9 months in the placebo group (HR 0.52; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.64; P<0.001).
The addition of pembrolizumab to standard chemotherapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival.

pico.population: 616 patients with untreated metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC

records.title: Effects of Aspirin for Primary Prevention in Persons with Diabetes Mellitus

passages.text: The balance of benefits and bleeding risks associated with aspirin for primary cardiovascular prevention in diabetes remains controversial.
We randomly assigned 15,480 adults with diabetes but no evident cardiovascular disease to receive aspirin 100 mg daily or matching placebo.
During a mean follow-up of 7.4 years, serious vascular events occurred in 658 participants (8.5%) on aspirin versus 743 (9.6%) on placebo (rate ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.79 to 0.97; P=0.01).
Major bleeding events occurred in 314 participants (4.1%) on aspirin compared to 245 (3.2%) on placebo (rate ratio 1.29; 95% CI 1.09 to 1.52; P=0.003).
Aspirin prevented serious vascular events in persons who had diabetes and no evident cardiovascular disease, but it also caused major bleeding events.

pico.population: 15,480 adults with diabetes without cardiovascular disease
pico.outcome: Serious vascular events vs major bleeding

records.title: Remdesivir for 5 or 10 Days in Patients with Severe Covid-19

passages.text: Remdesivir has in vitro antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, but the optimal treatment course is undefined.
In a randomized open-label trial, hospitalized patients with severe Covid-19 without mechanical ventilation received intravenous remdesivir for either 5 days or 10 days.
A total of 397 patients were randomized (200 for 5 days, 197 for 10 days).
At day 14, clinical improvement of 2 points or more on an ordinal scale occurred in 64% of patients in the 5-day group and in 54% in the 10-day group (P=0.14 after baseline adjustment).
In patients with severe Covid-19 not requiring mechanical ventilation, our trial did not demonstrate a significant difference between a 5-day and a 10-day course of remdesivir.

pico.population: 397 hospitalized patients with severe Covid-19 not ventilated

records.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir for High-Risk, Nonhospitalized Adults with Covid-19

passages.text: Nirmatrelvir is an orally administered SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitor with in vitro activity.

In this phase 2-3 trial, symptomatic nonhospitalized adults at high risk for progression were assigned to receive 300 mg of nirmatrelvir plus 100 mg of ritonavir or placebo every 12 hours for 5 days within 5 days after symptom onset.
A total of 2246 patients underwent randomization.
Covid-19-related hospitalization or death by day 28 occurred in 0.77% of patients in the nirmatrelvir group compared to 6.31% in the placebo group, an 89.1% relative reduction (P<0.001).
Treatment of symptomatic Covid-19 with nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir resulted in an 89% lower risk of progression to severe illness than placebo.

pico.population: 2246 symptomatic high-risk nonhospitalized adults with Covid-19
pico.intervention: Nirmatrelvir (300 mg) plus ritonavir (100 mg) BID for 5 days

records.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis

passages.text: Large trials have shown cardiovascular benefits with SGLT2 inhibitors, but degree of consistency across drug classes and patient subgroups remains unclear.
We systematically searched PubMed for randomized placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcome trials of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes through October 2017.
Three trials comprising 34,322 patients (EMPA-REG, CANVAS, and DECLARE-TIMI 58) were included.

SGLT2 inhibitors reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 11% (HR 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83 to 0.96; P=0.001) and reduced composite cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure by 23% (HR 0.77; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.84; P<0.001).
SGLT2 inhibitors have moderate benefits on major adverse cardiovascular events and robust benefits in reducing heart failure hospitalization.

pico.population: 34,322 patients with type 2 diabetes across 3 RCTs

records.title: International Evaluation of an AI System for Breast Cancer Screening

passages.text: Mammography screening reduces breast cancer mortality, but high false-positive and false-negative rates pose ongoing challenges.

We developed an artificial intelligence system and evaluated its diagnostic accuracy on retrospective screening mammograms from 25,856 women in the United Kingdom and 3,097 women in the United States.
The AI system demonstrated an absolute reduction of 5.7% in false positives and 9.4% in false negatives in the US dataset.
The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for the AI system was 0.740 in the UK and 0.889 in the US, outperforming historical individual radiologist averages.
An artificial intelligence system successfully identified breast cancer from screening mammograms with accuracy superior to individual human experts.

pico.population: 28,953 screening mammograms from UK and US cohorts
pico.outcome: AUC, false positive, and false negative rates

records.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and CKD Progression in Diabetic Nephropathy

passages.text: Dietary interventions may slow renal decline in type 2 diabetes mellitus, but long-term longitudinal data are limited.

In a prospective cohort of 984 adults with type 2 diabetes and early-stage diabetic nephropathy, dietary adherence was assessed with a validated 14-item Mediterranean diet questionnaire over a median of 5.8 years.
Higher Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with a 28% reduced risk of eGFR decline > 30% (multivariate HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.54 to 0.95; P=0.02).
No significant difference in progression to end-stage renal disease was observed (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.58 to 1.34; P=0.56).
Higher adherence to a Mediterranean diet was associated with slower eGFR decline in diabetic nephropathy, though observational confounding cannot be excluded.

pico.population: 984 adults with T2D and diabetic nephropathy

records.title: Tocilizumab in Hospitalized Patients with Severe Covid-19 Pneumonia

passages.text: Coronavirus disease 2019 is associated with immune dysregulation and elevated interleukin-6 levels.
In a randomized trial, 452 hospitalized patients with severe Covid-19 pneumonia were assigned (2:1) to receive tocilizumab (8 mg/kg) or placebo in addition to standard care.
Clinical status at day 28 did not differ significantly between tocilizumab and placebo (median ordinal score 1.0 vs 2.0; odds ratio for improvement 1.19; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.76; P=0.36).
Mortality at day 28 was 19.7% in the tocilizumab group and 19.4% in the placebo group (difference 0.3 percentage points; 95% CI -7.6 to 8.2).
In this trial involving hospitalized patients with severe Covid-19 pneumonia, tocilizumab did not result in significantly better clinical status or lower mortality than placebo at 28 days.

pico.population: 452 hospitalized patients with severe Covid-19 pneumonia
pico.outcome: Clinical status score and mortality at day 28

records.title: Effect of Hydroxychloroquine on Covid-19 Postexposure Prophylaxis

passages.text: Whether hydroxychloroquine prevents Covid-19 illness after high-risk or moderate-risk exposure is unknown.
We conducted a randomized trial evaluating hydroxychloroquine as postexposure prophylaxis within 4 days after household or healthcare exposure in 821 asymptomatic adults.

The incidence of new illness compatible with Covid-19 did not differ significantly between participants receiving hydroxychloroquine (49 of 414 [11.8%]) and those receiving placebo (58 of 407 [14.3%]); absolute difference -2.4 percentage points (95% CI, -7.0 to 2.2; P=0.35).
Side effects were more common with hydroxychloroquine than with placebo (40.1% vs 16.8%), but no serious adverse events occurred.
After high-risk or moderate-risk exposure to Covid-19, hydroxychloroquine did not prevent illness or PCR-confirmed infection when used within 4 days.

pico.population: 821 asymptomatic adults after moderate-to-high risk Covid-19 exposure
pico.outcome: Incidence of Covid-19 illness within 14 days

records.title: SYNTHETIC: Prospective Adaptive Protocol for Sepsis Resuscitation (No Results Reported)
records.journal: Fictional Journal of Critical Care Protocols
records.notes: Tests whether evaluator and summarizer correctly output 'Not reported in the abstract.' for missing findings and outcome metrics.

passages.text: Severe sepsis carries high in-hospital mortality, and fluid resuscitation strategies remain variable across intensive care units.
To describe the design of an ongoing randomized adaptive trial evaluating dynamic microvascular perfusion-guided resuscitation.
A total of 800 planned patients across 12 intensive care units are being randomized to protocolized perfusion-guided resuscitation versus standard surviving sepsis guidelines.
Participant enrollment began in January 2025, and interim efficacy analyses will take place after 400 patients are enrolled.
Trial enrollment is ongoing, and definitive efficacy and mortality outcomes will be reported upon trial completion.

pico.population: 800 planned patients with severe sepsis across 12 ICUs

records.title: SYNTHETIC: Circulating Biomarker Delta and Atherosclerotic Event Risk (Inconclusive Findings)
records.notes: Tests preservation of inconclusive conclusions and unadjusted vs adjusted contradictory associations.

passages.text: Elevated plasma levels of Biomarker Delta have been hypothesized to accelerate coronary plaque instability.
We followed 1,420 asymptomatic middle-aged adults for 6 years, recording incident myocardial infarction and stroke.
In unadjusted univariate regression, upper-quartile Biomarker Delta was associated with increased cardiovascular events (HR 1.62; 95% CI 1.18 to 2.22; P=0.003).

However, after comprehensive adjustment for systolic blood pressure, smoking, and LDL cholesterol, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant (adjusted HR 1.09; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.47; P=0.58).
The findings are inconclusive regarding Biomarker Delta as an independent causal risk factor, and routine clinical screening is currently not supported.

pico.population: 1,420 asymptomatic middle-aged adults followed for 6 years

records.title: SYNTHETIC: Gene Replacement in Ultra-Rare Pediatric Dystrophy (Small Sample Size n=6)
records.test_category: Synthetic - Very Small Sample Size Edge Case
records.notes: Tests whether summary preserves exact small sample size n=6 without inflating to broad population claims.

passages.text: Type-IV mitochondrial neurodegenerative dystrophy is an ultra-rare fatal disorder with no approved therapies.
A single-arm pilot safety study administered intrathecal AAV9-MND1 gene therapy to 6 pediatric patients aged 2 to 7 years.
At 12 months, 4 of 6 patients demonstrated stabilization on the Gross Motor Function Scale, while 2 patients experienced transient asymptomatic hepatic transaminase elevation.
Intrathecal AAV9-MND1 demonstrated manageable safety and preliminary motor stabilization in this 6-patient cohort, warranting multi-center expansion.

pico.population: 6 pediatric patients aged 2 to 7 years with rare dystrophy
pico.outcome: Motor stabilization and safety at 12 months

records.title: SYNTHETIC: Multi-Arm Dosing of Novel Anticoagulant Factor-XIa Inhibitor (Dense Numerical Results)
records.notes: Tests high-density numerical extraction: percentages, dosing tiers, hazard ratios, relative risk reductions, and p-values.

passages.text: In a double-blind trial, 1,840 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomized to oral Factor-XIa inhibitor Compound-Z (25 mg, 50 mg, or 100 mg twice daily) or enoxaparin 40 mg once daily.

Venous thromboembolism occurred in 14.8% of patients on 25 mg (relative risk 0.82; 95% CI 0.65 to 1.04; P=0.10), 8.2% on 50 mg (relative risk 0.46; 95% CI 0.33 to 0.63; P<0.001), and 4.1% on 100 mg (relative risk 0.23; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.36; P<0.001), compared to 17.9% with enoxaparin.
Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding occurred in 2.2% with 25 mg, 2.5% with 50 mg, 3.8% with 100 mg, and 3.4% with enoxaparin.
Oral Compound-Z at 50 mg and 100 mg twice daily demonstrated superior antithrombotic efficacy compared to enoxaparin without increasing bleeding rates.
